title: What is special about the number 142857?
description: The number one four two eight five seven is multiplied by one to seven, and its digits cycle round in a circle until the seventh product is all nines. Keeko doubts that seven times the number is one million.
teaching_notes: One idea: the products of the repeating block cycle round the same six digits. Watch for children who round the seventh product up to one million.

source: Multiply 142857 by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7. What do you notice?
video_script.why: The child has found that one divided by seven repeats the block one four two eight five seven, and now multiplies that block to see what it does.
video_script.substitution: the book's own seven multiplications of the block by one to seven
video_script.anchor: The number one four two eight five seven, multiplied by one, two, three, four, five, six and seven
video_script.wrong_answer: seven times the number is one million
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip says seven times the number is one million, because the number is about one seventh of a million. The last digit of the product is nine, so the product cannot be a million.
video_script.payoff_line: The products cycle round, and seven times the number gives all nines.

final_answer.spoken: the digits cycle round for one to six, and seven times the number is nine nine nine nine nine nine

maths_rules: each product has the same six digits in the same circular order, starting at a different digit
video_script.design: One idea: the products of the block cycle round the same six digits, and the seventh product is all nines. Assumes the block from one divided by seven. Wrong idea: rounding the seventh product up to one million. The number stays all video; the circle stays through the ground; the seventh product appears only on the answer beat.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, multiply by seven, from the right. Seven times seven is forty nine. Write nine and carry four.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Seven times five is thirty five, and with four that is thirty nine. Write nine and carry three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Seven times eight is fifty six, and with three that is fifty nine. Write nine and carry five.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Seven times two is fourteen, and with five that is nineteen. Write nine and carry one.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Seven times four is twenty eight, and with one that is twenty nine. Write nine and carry two. Seven times one is seven, and two more is nine.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks seven times the number is one million.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But seven times seven is forty nine, so the last digit is nine, not zero.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The product is one less than a million, and that is all nines.
